discovery: Electron spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent single-spin quantum control

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed encoding quantum information in the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot, with gates driven by electrically controlled exchange. DiVincenzo's criteria became the benchmark for any physical quantum computer. Vandersypen and colleagues then turned the proposal into physics: single-shot readout of an individual electron spin, coherent single-spin rotations by electron spin resonance and electric fields, and high-fidelity two-qubit gates in silicon that now pass fault-tolerance thresholds. Together this work showed that the quantum state of one electron spin in a solid can be prepared, controlled and measured with precision, and that it stays coherent in a technologically mature host. It founded an entire field, now spanning gate-defined and donor qubits worldwide, and opened a credible, scalable route from fundamental spin physics to quantum processors built with semiconductor manufacturing.
